title: TCP congestion control, in RFC 5681, is four algorithms: slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery
summary: TCP congestion control, in RFC 5681, is four algorithms: slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery.
body: RFC 5681 defines TCP's four intertwined congestion-control algorithms as slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery. The source says: "Blanton Purdue University September 2009 TCP Congestion Control Abstract This document defines TCP's four intertwined congestion control algorithms: slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery." These algorithms are how a TCP sender is specified to respond to the network. They are not a promise of a particular throughput. The names are the RFC's, including 'slow start,' which is the name of the algorithm and not a description of a user's experience.
